sources.title: Robert Arlt and Monica Zin: Kanaganahalli (or Sannathi)
sources.note: Direct full scholarly entry: chronology, Ashokan edicts at Chandralamba temple, later Satavahana architecture and relief dates, historical Ashoka depiction. Public atlas assertions separately verified by decoded geography.

sources.title: NCERT: Kings, Farmers and Towns, section 2.1
sources.note: Indexed institutional textbook text: gana/sangha oligarchies and varied mahajanapada lists. Same chapter already used in Magadha; count all runtime usage and override conservatively. Direct page temporarily fails.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Bharat SHRI: Brahmagiri and Bhattiprolu inscriptions
sources.note: Direct gallery entries: Brahmagiri Prakrit/Brahmi third century BCE, administrative chain and moral precepts; Bhattiprolu caskets circa third-second centuries BCE, unknown dynasty and Kubhiraka. Shared URL with existing Chauhans drama entry, budget combined. Do not adopt gallery’s unrelated script inconsistencies or pre-Ashokan superlative.

sources.title: B. K. Thapar: Maski 1954, Ancient India 13 (1957)
sources.note: Indexed original pp.6-7, Previous work: C. Beadon mining prospecting and 1915 edict discovery; reading includes personal name Ashoka. Full PDF fetch failed/timed out and was cancelled. No old absolute archaeological chronology adopted.

sources.title: Peter G. Johansen and Andrew M. Bauer: Maski Archaeological Research Project
sources.note: Direct 2013 primary project report: introduction and Preliminary results,15 ha Early Historic settlement, gold-processing slicks/MARP-8, edict proximity and explicitly tentative political interpretation.

sources.title: Andrew M. Bauer and Peter G. Johansen: The politics and historicity of megalithic places in early South India
sources.note: Direct full 2023 primary study, research-history and MARP sections. Megalith building spans several periods; cereals/pulses and herds, Iron Age/Early Historic manuring interpretation, collective activities and social affiliation. Avoid predating specific Neolithic cemetery data to the card period.

sources.title: Puratattva35: Significant Discoveries around Sudarshan Lake, Junagadh
sources.note: Indexed original article opening identifies later Girnar inscriptions as evidence for Chandragupta-era Pushyagupta reservoir and Ashoka-era Tushaspa improvements. Use as later retrospective testimony; no unsupported exact reconstructed lake dimensions.

sources.title: Edgar Thurston: The Madras Presidency, with Mysore, Coorg and the Associated States
sources.note: Indexed original printed p.148, fig.52 and discussion of Bhattiprolu caskets; Kura’s father/mother and Kura among supporters. Cross-check Epigraphia Indica X appendix nos.1329-1330 (indexed primary) and Fleet 1908 p.101 note1. No uncertain donor Siva reading required.

sources.title: Heather Walder: Inscription Carving Technology of Early Historic South Asia
sources.note: Direct author-uploaded scholarly chapter, Walking with the Unicorn (2018), pp.605-622. Exact Roman Chapaḍena likhite and supplied translation on printed 615; only lipikarena is Kharoshthi. Experimental methods pp.608-614 and field assessment 615-619. Modern reproduction is not an ancient object.

proposedOverrides.name: Hindu kingdoms and republics
proposedOverrides.summary: A changing regional atlas umbrella, including places later subject to Mauryan imperial authority.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: New focused contextual narrative, one exact ID and no aliases. The existing hindu-kingdoms card covers 500 BCE-800 CE with much later examples and is not an adequate phase-specific shared card.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: 323-300 BCE has Deccan bbox[72.7585,11.3468,84.2462,23.4144] and western/northwestern bbox[67.4845,20.6509,77.6294,31.4756].300-200 BCE retains only the identical Deccan polygon. Detailed topology/point checks saved separately.
batchIdentityNotes.sites: Maski, Brahmagiri, Sannati, Bhattiprolu, Dharanikota insideDeccan; Girnar insideonlyfirstoutline. Taxila, Sagala, Ujjain, Sanchi, Pauni, Adam, Dhauli, Madurai outside. No assertion of identified regional assemblies from geometry.
batchIdentityNotes.historicalLimit: Early third-century/Mauryan expansion not reflected by static polygon. Regional religion label is insufficient; no universal Hindu identity or uniform republic claimed. Later Satavahana reliefs and retrospective Girnar evidence labeled later.
batchIdentityNotes.related: Magadha, Maurya, Kosala, Kuru, Gandhara, earlier Hindu kingdoms and modern/medieval Rajput records remain separate. No faith-based aliasing.
batchIdentityNotes.researchLimit: No securely contextualized household medicine/toilet evidence established for this particular interval; not invented. Broad regional subsistence and manuring evidence labelled appropriately. Transliteration preserves attested Prakrit but does not reconstruct ancient handwriting.
